end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified ways to measure distance, including maps or online searches.
Practised links between distance, fuel use, pollution, refrigeration, and electricity.
Suggested local food as one way to reduce food miles; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised defining food miles and explaining how transport distance can affect fuel use, pollution, freshness, and refrigeration. Rohan correctly identified that choosing local food can save fuel and reduce pollution, and the idea that imported food is automatically better was addressed during the lesson. At home, ask them to compare two foods by finding where each came from and discussing which travelled farther.
